rows.title: 1. Files and syntax — Comments
rows.summary: `//` starts a comment.
body: `//` starts a comment. To continue it on another line, the line starts with ` * `: the `*` goes right below the
second `/` of the `//`, as in a JavaScript or Java `/** */` comment. That way it stands apart from the code at a
glance. In VS Code, pressing Enter inside a comment is enough: the new line already has its ` * `; a second Enter
on an empty ` * ` line ends the comment. Comments stay in place in the generated code.
A line more indented than the `//` without ` * ` is error `N0021`, with its fix.

rows.title: NuclearLang — Base language v0.1 (draft) — 6.1 Operators (lowest to highest precedence)
body: - `==` is always a strict comparison. There is no `===`.
- `x is User` checks whether `x` is of type `User`.
- `x as Type` converts the type: `data = read(file) as <string, int>`.
- `value!` asserts that the value is not null: `user.address!.city`. The `!` goes right after a name, `)` or
`]`. Before a value, `!` is an error: write `not`.
- `a / b` is always a decimal division; `a ~/ b` drops the decimals (toward zero). `%`, the bitwise operators and
the integer width are the target's: TypeScript's `%` keeps the dividend's sign and its bitwise operators work on
32 bits; Dart's `%` is never negative and its integers have 64 bits.
- The bitwise operators bind tighter than the comparisons (unlike C): `flags & READ != 0` is `(flags & READ) != 0`.
`~` is await, so the complement is `^x`. Compound forms: `%=`, `&=`, `|=`, `^=`, `<<=`, `>>=`, `>>>=`.
- `x in xs` asks whether a list contains `x`; with a map, whether it has the key `x`.
- Nuclear has no standard library of its own: math, text, regular expressions, collections, dates, JSON, bytes
and async come from the target (`Math.sqrt` in TypeScript, `sqrt` of `dart:math` in Dart), imported
automatically. `examples/stdlib/` has one program per area and target that prints the same result in both
(`tools/stdlib-check.sh` runs them); `nuclear help operations` lists them.

body: `kind`, `modifier` and `clause` words **are not reserved in Nuclear**. They only mean something in the
header of a declaration, and the parser accepts them without knowing them ("header + block" rule, see
nuclear-base.md §4). The active dialect validates them (`N0201`, `N0202`):
extension NumberParsing on String  // kind + name + clause
Outside the header they are normal identifiers: `extension = "png"` is a valid variable (and if it
collides in the target, it is renamed).
